```sh
resolves https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/issues/6"

```

comments.content: Hi @gentlementlegen good luck! I encountered a chicken-and-egg problem for Knip reporter part here: https://github.com/ubiquity/keygen.ubq.fi/pull/5#discussion_r1530367166 , still experimenting on that..

You may want to read a few links from that thread. Basically, for branches across the same repository it does work correctly with pull_request, https://github.com/gitcoindev/keygen.ubq.fi/actions/runs/8355152504
In case of `pull_request` workflow opened from a forked repository , the `secrets` are not passed (all of the variables are `None` / null`) , there are ways to deal with this but I have not found the perfect solution, yet.

My last version that 'almost works' is to use pull_request_workflow and a fine grained token https://github.com/korrrba/keygen.ubq.fi/actions/runs/8366591693/workflow , see  tibdex/github-app-token@v2.1.0 . But perhaps I leave more investigation to you, you may discover something that works better. For the deploy workflow @rndquu was able to solve it in an elegant way, building with read only permissions and deploying with the elevated ones.

Yes I have similar conclusions. By the way in one of the articles I found a hack that allows to workaround for `uses the base branch for the workflows ` default scenario:
```
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
```
When the `github.event.pull_request` is available, head.sha can be used to fetch the pull request workspace instead of the base branch.

I also thought about this approach, but for the Knip case two write permissions are needed:
```
permissions:
  checks: write
  issues: write
```
If we skip comments, `Checks: write` is the blocking one as well.  I began to wonder if there is a completely another way to tackle this like rewriting the knip-reporter to not to use checks -) I hope that @gentlementlegen can come up with a better solution.

There is a quite long thread in GitHub actions repository, https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/518
Many projects struggle with that. One of the last comments mentions the similar workflow that @rndquu introduced:
https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/518#issuecomment-1972009337
(does not work for Knip-reporter currently though due to https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter/blob/main/src/main.ts#L24 and the fact that it complains about `workflow_run`) . Perhaps this can be solved in the knip-reporter somehow.

comments.content:
[This](https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter/blob/1d32edf5aecf8728aae419758f2f4b4e35fd6945/src/main.ts#L24) check is introduced because PR number is used [here](https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter/blob/1d32edf5aecf8728aae419758f2f4b4e35fd6945/src/main.ts#L47).
The thing is that on `workflow_run` (which runs in a privileged context with access to secrets) we can still fetch associated PR number [this](https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/blob/05cf678961b481e76c21b95679c17ec9d3b33c23/action.yml#L41-L57) way. 
We could update https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter/blob/1d32edf5aecf8728aae419758f2f4b4e35fd6945/src/main.ts to work with `workflow_run` with (relatively) small code changes.

This all started with https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter, I would remove it, keep using plain `yarn knip` in a build workflow (which throws on knip warnings) and be done with that without refactoring https://github.com/Codex-/knip-reporter, introducing environments and other unnecessary stuff
We don't need sensitive credentials anywhere, the only ones I can think of are cloudflare credentials but they are already used [safely](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/cd49591bd37a0d616a0d1ea757b9c0e478ae0778/.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
I'm sure there is a way to mock github oauth without passing sensitive credentials in a build step

Right now there are only 2 places left which uses `pull_request_target` across `ubiquity` and `ubiquibot` organizations:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/onboard.ubq.fi/blob/902ff2b5c4116044f12fa266a0ab3e44315c0fcb/.github/workflows/knip.yml#L4
- https://github.com/ubiquity/onboard.ubq.fi/blob/902ff2b5c4116044f12fa266a0ab3e44315c0fcb/.github/workflows/cypress-testing.yml#L4

Right now we're using `pull_request_target` in many places like:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/blob/c553d5a7866c1ef76d4f589d8095c8bb751cbd49/.github/workflows/bun-testing.yml#L4
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ts-template/blob/84d03ca4fef2d5cf1ecff4bf1333e56895685151/.github/workflows/jest-testing.yml#L4
In the examples mentioned above workflows always check out the `development` branch + open a security hole for exfiltrating of github access token with write permissions.
Check this for more info:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/keygen.ubq.fi/pull/5#discussion_r1530367166
- https://github.com/ubiquity/cloudflare-deploy-action/issues/1#issuecomment-1999654318
What should be done:
- refactor all CI workflows in the https://github.com/ubiquity organization from `pull_request_target` to `pull_request`
- fix related CI errors where necessary
